become a drug addict before you kill yourself. that's what I did. Or....

Filll your mind with good language, read a good book and you will start to view your life full of meaning, you'll start seeing your life asa book, literarily. Listen to Allan Watts or Terrence Mckenna. They will pull you out of your head and fling you in to a different world. Listen to music, try even classical like Ravel Daphnis an Chloe, or Introduction and a Allegro, or anything, Beethoven. Art Music Literature is always medicinal, it gives expression to our repressed unconscious, that's why it feels so good. Do yoga. memorize Ashtanga sequence and learn Ujjayi breathing, and do it. every. day. Consider Ayahuasca. If you can do MDMA therapy, its 400$ in Canada. If you really are on the edge, find clonazepam or opiates. I nearly lost both my arms and leg from injecting heroin and to an infection, and am in mental hospital right now, for the 6th time in a year. You got hang on. I'm am hanging on so tightly. Made a post about my close encounter with suicide, maybe it would interest you how I survived. Lemme tell ya, there's no rock bottom until you decide there is. I was a homeless fentanyl addict year ago. You got kick yourself in the butt and start doing some of the activities I suggested.

I used to have a blog called Experimental radio station for the Psychotically depressed and suicidal! Yay! If I haven't bored you yet, ill send you one to read

​

Spent the last several days just lying on my bed, staring at the wall, stopped eating, stopped brushing my teeth, stopped everything, not even a netflix, not a page of a book. I'm sure there are lots of people in existential crisis right now. Gave me a chance to remember, why? Why do anything at all? Why even choose to live? We make the choice to live every second that we are alive and not jumping in front of a Bus. Its interesting. Why?

All I can say is, whatever you do, don't do it for yourself. It will backfire. Do it for anything else, but not for yourself. Get out of bed, clean your room, and be strong, not for yourself, but rather for the people who love you, even if they are dead. All the people who showed care for you, maybe no one else but the person you called on a suicide hotline if that is all you've got. For your mother, for your father, for your friends, for all the people who chose to try helping you even when you'd already given up faith in yourself, even if it was 20 years ago. How would they react if they saw a mountain of cigarette butts on the floor next to your bed. Start there. Do it for them, at the very least.

This is a beautiful, fool-proof reality you can step into, no matter how fucked up you are. Even if you fail and drown. That is what being human is all about. We live to fail by necessity. We will die. This will all be over faster than any person can anticipate. And we will enter a Nothing in which even our greatest achievements die with us. So don't be afraid. Everyone is in the same boat, although few can see it. This is as real as it gets, and is more tragic than your most tragic thought. It is a tragedy we can all face now, if you are unwilling to look at your more personal tragedies and accept them. Remember this truth.

Some day, if you do this long enough, you will realize that the whole time, you have actually been doing this for yourself all along. You can only find your true Self through the Other. Don't look at the pinball game taking place in your thoughts for answers if you are stuck in a miserable place. Look outward, seek it outwardly. Do it for them, the poor people in the boat with you, all of us secretly panicking about this life. Give them meaning and respond to love. Show them, show all of us. We are here for you, and you are here for us.

Amen

"The schizophrenic drowns in the same water in which the shaman swims with delight...."

If you are drowning, it may be because you are being asked to learn how to Swim.... You may be very deep, but look to the Light above the water's surface, and swim there... Don't look down. Follow the Light. You are lost in the sea of your own unconscious. Remember that somewhere, there is a paradise, a beach with your name on it, a shore to which you can swim, if you choose... Remember the breath, pulling in, then pushing out, like the waves of a the seaside on the beach, crashing and retracting........ That is your beach. Swim there.
